output.brief:
The rejects come from an interaction, not from any single party. Arnholt resin arrives wetter (about 0.27–0.33% moisture, against a 0.20% molding limit) and the Press 5 dryer (D5) is degraded, so it can't dry it enough. Arnholt through D5 gives about 10% rejects. Arnholt through Press 7's healthy dryer gives 0.8%. Quillan through D5 gives 0.9%. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 gave 0.8% rejects. The new operators are not the cause. Their reject rates match the experienced operators' on each resin. The higher second-shift rate only reflects that second-shift VX runs entirely on Press 5. Don't discipline the operators, and don't drop Arnholt outright.

Do this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore its original alarm limit, and verify the dew point is back to −40 °C. Until then keep Arnholt off D5. Add a moisture check at the press for every resin lot. Open question: Arnholt's wetter arrival may be due to storage in the unconditioned north annex or to the supplier, and the evidence can't separate the two. Test that before paying for warehouse space. Confidence is high on the main finding.
